description: India outbound education remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS): annual cap and tax collected at source (TCS). Draft: secondary sources only. Check every rule against RBI and Income Tax Department sources before relying on it.

lrs_annual_cap_usd.unit: USD per individual per financial year (April to March)
lrs_annual_cap_usd.check_against: RBI LRS FAQs and Master Direction
lrs_annual_cap_usd.note: Checked 18 Oct 2026 against the primary text. RBI Master Direction - Liberalised Remittance Scheme (updated 6 Sep 2024): 'Authorised Dealers may freely allow remittances by resident individuals up to USD 2,50,000 per Financial Year (April-March)'; the limit includes current account remittances such as studies abroad.
lrs_annual_cap_usd.previous_source: Chandan's own research document (India Cross-Border Remittance, May 2026)

tcs_threshold_inr.unit: INR per PAN per financial year
tcs_threshold_inr.check_against: Income-tax Act 2025 s.394(1), Table Sl. 7-8 (was 1961 Act s.206C(1G)); Finance Act 2026
tcs_threshold_inr.note: Checked 18 Oct 2026 against the primary text. Income-tax Act 2025 s.394(1), Table Sl. 7: 'Remittance under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme of an amount or aggregate of the amounts exceeding ten lakh rupees', collected by the authorised dealer.

tcs_threshold_aggregates_all_purposes.check_against: Income-tax Act 2025 s.394(1), Table Sl. 7-8 (was 1961 Act s.206C(1G)); Finance Act 2026
tcs_threshold_aggregates_all_purposes.note: Checked 18 Oct 2026 against the primary text. s.394(1) Table Sl. 7 is one row for all LRS remittances, with the threshold on 'an amount or aggregate of the amounts'.

tcs_rate_education_self_funded.unit: rate on the amount above the threshold
tcs_rate_education_self_funded.check_against: Income-tax Act 2025 s.394(1), Table Sl. 7-8 (was 1961 Act s.206C(1G)); Finance Act 2026
tcs_rate_education_self_funded.note: Checked 18 Oct 2026 against the primary text. s.394(1) Table Sl. 7(a): 2% 'for purposes of education or medical treatment' (20% for other purposes); the 5% to 2% cut was announced in the Budget 2026-27 speech. Page last reviewed by the department on 8 Oct 2026.

tcs_rate_education_loan_funded.check_against: Income-tax Act 2025 s.394(1), Table Sl. 7-8 (was 1961 Act s.206C(1G)); Finance Act 2026
tcs_rate_education_loan_funded.note: Checked 18 Oct 2026 against the primary text. s.394(4)(b): no collection 'if the amount being remitted out is a loan obtained from any financial institution as defined in section 129(3)(b), for the purpose of pursuing any education'.

tcs_rate_no_pan.unit: rate on the amount above the threshold
tcs_rate_no_pan.check_against: Income-tax Act 2025 provision replacing 1961 Act s.206CC
tcs_rate_no_pan.note: Checked 18 Oct 2026 against the primary text. s.397(2)(b)(ii): without a valid PAN, tax is collected 'at the higher of the following rates, not exceeding 20%': twice the rate, or 5%. For education at 2% that is 5%.

tcs_prior_other_purposes_count_toward_th.note: Checked 18 Oct 2026 against the primary text: s.394(1) Table Sl. 7 counts the 'aggregate of the amounts' remitted under LRS, which supports this, but the Act does not state it for mixed purposes in so many words. Kept unverified until a bank confirms.

tcs_base_excludes_fees.note: TCS is computed on the remitted amount, not on fees. Confirm with a bank. Checked 18 Oct 2026 against the primary text: s.394 does not say how bank fees are treated; still needs a bank's confirmation.

gst_on_service_charge.note: GST applies to conversion and remittance service charges. The rate is taken from each route's own fee schedule.

lrs_purpose_studies_abroad_permitted.check_against: RBI Master Direction - Liberalised Remittance Scheme (updated 6 Sep 2024); FEMA (Current Account Transactions) Rules 2000, Schedule III para 1
lrs_purpose_studies_abroad_permitted.note: Checked 19 Oct 2026 against the primary text. Master Direction para 7 lists 'studies abroad' among the current account transactions available to resident individuals under Para 1 of Schedule III, subsumed under the LRS limit. TuitionPilot only pays invoices whose purpose is education.

lrs_pan_mandatory.check_against: RBI Master Direction - Liberalised Remittance Scheme (updated 6 Sep 2024)
lrs_pan_mandatory.note: Checked 19 Oct 2026 against the primary text. Master Direction para 16: 'It is mandatory for the resident individual to provide his/her Permanent Account Number (PAN)' for remittances under the Scheme. Without a PAN the bank should not process the remittance; tcs_rate_no_pan is kept only to show the cost if one is missing.

lrs_form_a2_required.check_against: RBI Master Direction - Liberalised Remittance Scheme (updated 6 Sep 2024)
lrs_form_a2_required.note: Checked 19 Oct 2026 against the primary text. Master Direction para 15: the resident individual 'should furnish Form A2' for purchase of foreign exchange under LRS, and designates one AD bank branch for remittances under the Scheme. TuitionPilot drafts an A2-style form; the bank's own A2 must be signed and submitted.

lrs_studies_above_cap_on_institution_est.check_against: RBI Master Direction - Liberalised Remittance Scheme (updated 6 Sep 2024)
lrs_studies_above_cap_on_institution_est.note: Checked 19 Oct 2026 against the primary text. Master Direction para 7(h): for studies abroad, AD banks may allow amounts exceeding USD 2,50,000 'based on the estimate received from the institution abroad'. TuitionPilot does not apply this itself: a payment above the cap is escalated to the family and their bank.

aml_sanctions_screening.check_against: RBI Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, as amended: para 10(9) (customer acceptance) and para 51 (UNSC lists under Section 51A of the UAPA, 1967)
aml_sanctions_screening.note: Seen 19 Oct 2026 on the RBI page (consolidated as on 12 Jul 2018): para 10(9) asks for a system to ensure 'the identity of the customer does not match with any person or entity' on the circulated sanctions lists; para 51 forbids accounts for those on the UNSC lists. Not yet checked against the current amended direction. TuitionPilot screens the remitter, the student and the payee against a SYNTHETIC list (data/screening/watchlist_synthetic.json); a real deployment must use the lists the bank is required to use.

lrs_source_of_funds_declared.check_against: RBI LRS Master Direction (Form A2 declaration) and the authorised dealer bank's own Form A2 / LRS application
lrs_source_of_funds_declared.note: Banks ask the remitter to declare where the money comes from on the LRS application and Form A2. TuitionPilot records the declaration on the A2-style draft; the exact wording and what proof the bank wants vary by bank. Not yet checked against a primary text.

tcs_living_costs_abroad_education_rate.check_against: Income-tax Act 2025 s.394(1), Table Sl. 7-8 (remittance under LRS for the purpose of education)
tcs_living_costs_abroad_education_rate.note: The student budget treats money sent for a student's living costs abroad as an education remittance (the self-funded education rate above the threshold). Whether a bank treats rent and maintenance as 'education' or as another LRS purpose, with a different TCS rate, needs a bank's confirmation.
